verses.zh: 他又带我回到圣地朝东的外门；那门关闭了。
verses.en: Then he brought me back by way of the outer gate of the sanctuary that faces east, but it was shut.

verses.zh: 耶和华对我说：「这门必须关闭，不可敞开，谁也不可由其中进入；因为耶和华―以色列的　神已经由其中进入，所以必须关闭。
verses.en: The Lord said to me: “This gate will be shut; it will not be opened, and no one will enter by it. For the Lord, the God of Israel, has entered by it; therefore it will remain shut.

verses.zh: 至于王，他必按王的位分，坐在其内，在耶和华面前吃饼。他必由这门的廊而入，也必由此而出。」
verses.en: Only the prince may sit in it to eat a sacrificial meal[NOTE:1] before the Lord; he will enter by way of the porch of the gate and will go out by the same way.”
notes: Heb “to eat bread.”

verses.zh: 他又带我由北门来到殿前。我观看，见耶和华的荣光充满耶和华的殿，我就俯伏在地。
verses.en: Then he brought me by way of the north gate to the front of the temple. As I watched, I noticed[NOTE:1] the glory of the Lord filling the Lord’s temple, and I threw myself face down.
notes: The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.

verses.zh: 耶和华对我说：「人子啊，我对你所说耶和华殿中的一切典章法则，你要放在心上，用眼看，用耳听，并要留心殿宇和圣地一切出入之处。
verses.en: The Lord said to me: “Son of man, pay attention,[NOTE:1] watch closely, and listen carefully to[NOTE:2] everything I tell you concerning all the statutes of the Lord’s house and all its laws. Pay attention to the entrances[NOTE:3] to the temple with all the exits of the sanctuary.
notes: Heb “set your heart” (so also in the latter part of the verse).
Heb “Set your mind, look with your eyes, and with your ears hear.”
The Syriac, Vulgate, and Targum read the plural. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 2:618.

verses.zh: 你要对那悖逆的以色列家说，主耶和华如此说：以色列家啊，你们行一切可憎的事，当够了吧！
verses.en: Say to the rebellious,[NOTE:1] to the house of Israel, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: Enough of all your abominable practices, O house of Israel!
notes: The LXX reads “house of rebellion.”

verses.zh: 你们把我的食物，就是脂油和血献上的时候，将身心未受割礼的外邦人领进我的圣地，玷污了我的殿；又背了我的约，在你们一切可憎的事上，加上这一层。
verses.en: When you bring foreigners, those uncircumcised in heart and in flesh, into my sanctuary, you desecrate[NOTE:1] it—even my house—when you offer my food, the fat and the blood. You[NOTE:2] have broken my covenant by all your abominable practices.
notes: Heb “to desecrate.”
The Greek, Syriac, and Latin versions read “you.” The Masoretic text reads “they.”

verses.zh: 你们也没有看守我的圣物，却派别人在圣地替你们看守我所吩咐你们的。
verses.en: You have not kept charge of my holy things, but you have assigned foreigners[NOTE:1] to keep charge of my sanctuary for you.
notes: This word is not in the Hebrew text but is supplied from the context. tc Instead of an energic ו (nun), the text may have read a third masculine plural suffix ם (mem), “them,” which was confused with ן (nun) in the old script. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 2:621.

verses.zh: 「主耶和华如此说：以色列中的外邦人，就是身心未受割礼的，都不可入我的圣地。」
verses.en: This is what the Sovereign Lord says: No foreigner who is uncircumcised in heart and flesh among all the foreigners who are among the people of Israel will enter into my sanctuary.[NOTE:1]
notes: Tobiah, an Ammonite (Neh 13:8), was dismissed from the temple.

verses.zh: 「当以色列人走迷的时候，有利未人远离我，就是走迷离开我、随从他们的偶像，他们必担当自己的罪孽。
verses.en: “‘But the Levites who went far from me, straying off from me after their idols when Israel went astray, will be responsible for[NOTE:1] their sin.
notes: Heb “will bear.”

verses.zh: 然而他们必在我的圣地当仆役，照管殿门，在殿中供职；必为民宰杀燔祭牲和平安祭牲，必站在民前伺候他们。
verses.en: Yet they will be ministers in my sanctuary, having oversight at the gates of the temple, and serving the temple. They will slaughter the burnt offerings and the sacrifices for the people, and they will stand before them to minister to them.

verses.zh: 因为这些利未人曾在偶像前伺候这民，成了以色列家罪孽的绊脚石，所以我向他们起誓：他们必担当自己的罪孽。这是主耶和华说的。
verses.en: Because they used to minister to them before their idols and became a sinful obstacle[NOTE:1] to the house of Israel, consequently I have made a vow[NOTE:2] concerning them, declares the Sovereign Lord, that they will be responsible for[NOTE:3] their sin.
notes: Heb “a stumbling block of iniquity.” This is a unique phrase of the prophet Ezekiel (cf. also Ezek 7:19; 14:3, 4, 7; 18:30).
Heb “I lifted up my hand.”
Heb “will bear.”

verses.zh: 他们不可亲近我，给我供祭司的职分，也不可挨近我的一件圣物，就是至圣的物；他们却要担当自己的羞辱和所行可憎之事的报应。
verses.en: They will not come near me to serve me as priest, nor will they come near any of my holy things, the things that are most sacred. They will bear the shame of the abominable deeds they have committed.

verses.zh: 然而我要使他们看守殿宇，办理其中的一切事，并做其内一切当做之工。」
verses.en: Yet I will appoint them to keep charge of the temple, all its service, and all that will be done in it.

verses.zh: 「以色列人走迷离开我的时候，祭司利未人撒督的子孙仍看守我的圣所。他们必亲近我，事奉我，并且侍立在我面前，将脂油与血献给我。这是主耶和华说的。
verses.en: “‘But the Levitical priests, the descendants of Zadok[NOTE:1] who kept the charge of my sanctuary when the people of Israel went astray from me, will approach me to minister to me; they will stand before me to offer me the fat and the blood, declares the Sovereign Lord.
notes: Zadok was a descendant of Aaron through Eleazar (1 Chr 6:50-53) who served as a priest during David’s reign (2 Sam 8:17).

verses.zh: 他们必进入我的圣所，就近我的桌前事奉我，守我所吩咐的。
verses.en: They will enter my sanctuary and approach my table to minister to me; they will keep my charge.

verses.zh: 他们进内院门必穿细麻衣。在内院门和殿内供职的时候不可穿羊毛衣服。
verses.en: “‘When they enter the gates of the inner court, they must wear linen garments; they must not have any wool on them when they minister in the inner gates of the court and in the temple.

verses.zh: 他们头上要戴细麻布裹头巾，腰穿细麻布裤子；不可穿使身体出汗的衣服。
verses.en: Linen turbans will be on their heads and linen undergarments will be around their waists; they must not bind themselves with anything that causes sweat.

verses.zh: 他们出到外院的民那里，当脱下供职的衣服，放在圣屋内，穿上别的衣服，免得因圣衣使民成圣。
verses.en: When they go out to the outer court to the people, they must remove the garments they were ministering in and place them in the holy chambers; they must put on other garments so that they will not transmit holiness to the people with their garments.[NOTE:1]
notes: For a similar concept of transmitting holiness, see Exod 19:12-14; Lev 10:1-2; 2 Sam 6:7. Comparable laws concerning the priest are found in Lev 10 and 21.

verses.zh: 不可剃头，也不可容发绺长长，只可剪发。
verses.en: “‘They must not shave their heads[NOTE:1] nor let their hair grow long;[NOTE:2] they must only trim their heads.
notes: The shaving of the head was associated with mourning (Ezek 7:18).
Letting the hair grow was associated with taking a vow (Num 6:5; Acts 21:23-26).

verses.zh: 祭司进内院的时候都不可喝酒。
verses.en: No priest may drink wine when he enters the inner court.

verses.zh: 不可娶寡妇和被休的妇人为妻，只可娶以色列后裔中的处女，或是祭司遗留的寡妇。
verses.en: They must not marry a widow or a divorcee, but they may marry a virgin from the house of Israel[NOTE:1] or a widow who is a priest’s widow.
notes: Heb “from the offspring of the house of Israel.”

verses.zh: 他们要使我的民知道圣俗的分别，又使他们分辨洁净的和不洁净的。
verses.en: Moreover, they will teach my people the difference between the holy and the common and show them how to distinguish between the ceremonially unclean and the clean.[NOTE:1]
notes: This task was a fundamental role of the priest (Lev 10:10).

verses.zh: 有争讼的事，他们应当站立判断，要按我的典章判断。在我一切的节期必守我的律法、条例，也必以我的安息日为圣日。
verses.en: “‘In a controversy they will act as judges;[NOTE:1] they will judge according to my ordinances. They will keep my laws and my statutes regarding all my appointed festivals and will observe[NOTE:2] my Sabbaths.
notes: For a historical illustration of the priest carrying out this function, see 2 Chr 19:9-11.
Heb “sanctify, set apart.”

verses.zh: 他们不可挨近死尸沾染自己，只可为父亲、母亲、儿子、女儿、弟兄，和未嫁人的姊妹沾染自己。
verses.en: “‘They must not come near a dead person or they will be defiled;[NOTE:1] however, for father, mother, son, daughter, brother, or unmarried sister, they may defile themselves.
notes: This law was part of the legal code for priests (Lev 21:1-3).

verses.zh: 祭司洁净之后，必再计算七日。
verses.en: After a priest[NOTE:1] has become ceremonially clean, they[NOTE:2] must count off a period of seven days for him.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (the priest) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
One medieval Hebrew ms, the LXX, and the Syriac, along with Lev 15:13, 28, read the verb as singular.

verses.zh: 当他进内院，进圣所，在圣所中事奉的日子，要为自己献赎罪祭。这是主耶和华说的。
verses.en: On the day he enters the sanctuary into the inner court to serve in the sanctuary, he must offer his sin offering, declares the Sovereign Lord.

verses.zh: 「祭司必有产业，我是他们的产业。不可在以色列中给他们基业；我是他们的基业。
verses.en: “‘This will be their inheritance: I am their inheritance, and you must give them no property in Israel; I am their property.[NOTE:1]

verses.zh: 素祭、赎罪祭，和赎愆祭他们都可以吃，以色列中一切永献的物都要归他们。
verses.en: They may eat the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering, and every devoted thing in Israel will be theirs.

verses.zh: 首先初熟之物和一切所献的供物都要归给祭司。你们也要用初熟的麦子磨面给祭司；这样，福气就必临到你们的家了。
verses.en: The first of all the firstfruits and all contributions of any kind[NOTE:1] will be for the priests; you will also give to the priest the first portion of your dough, so that a blessing may rest on your house.
notes: Heb has in addition “from your contributions,” a repetition unnecessary in English.

verses.zh: 无论是鸟是兽，凡自死的，或是撕裂的，祭司都不可吃。」
verses.en: The priests will not eat any bird or animal that has died a natural death or was torn to pieces by a wild animal.[NOTE:1]
notes: For this law, see Lev 7:24 and 17:15. tn The words “by a wild animal” are not in the Hebrew text but have been supplied in the translation as a clarification of the circumstances.
